Parker 2002 quote verbatim. All five follow-on knockout sources in the note resolve with the stated dates (Gelling 2003-01-24, Conarello 2006-11-28, Longuet 2008-11, Yang 2011-06-01, Yu 2011-08-10). Gelling also states normal body weight with reduced adiposity on chow.

Kelly 2015 (PMID 25656305, epub 2015-03-02) quote verbatim (tilde glyph only); Gelling 2003 'supraphysiological glucagon levels', alpha-cell hyperplasia. Prospective same, direction_only. Kelly's dose-dependent aminotransferase rise is left uncharged as knockout silence; ALT is measurable in mice, so decision 4 could read it as askable silence (rule question).

Kazierad 2016 (PMID 27059951, epub 2016-05-12) both quotes verbatim; Yang 2011 (PMC3130710, 2011-06-01) 'adverse lipid changes' and 'amino acids, cholesterol, and bile acid' verbatim. Prospective; NCT01856595 results 2018-11-01 verified. strengthens on a same-after-same entry: decision 7 names strengthens only for a second miss.

Guzman 2017 (PMID 28371155, epub 2017-06-08) raw abstract carries the quote verbatim plus HFF +4.44% and ALT +10.7 U/L vs placebo; NCT02111096 (terminated) results 2018-04-24 verified. Conarello 2007 stated, on high-fat diet, decreased body weight and resistance to hepatic steatosis; patients gained weight and liver fat, the trial's key endpoint. Guzman attributes the harms to chronic antagonism, not to untested conditions, so #35/#72 do not rescue it; a stated prediction failed in the opposite direction (decisions 4, 11), sticky under 6, no tier 1-4 attenuation source. Liver fat is arguable (Longuet 2008 and Yang 2011 show reduced fatty-acid oxidation and raised lipogenesis in the knockout), but weight is a clean miss: decreased on HFD (Conarello), normal on chow (Gelling), up in patients. No earlier member weight or liver-fat datum (Kelly 2015, Kazda 2016, Kazda 2017 abstracts report none), so 2017 holds.

Zhou 2009 (Pancreas, PMID 19657311, PMC2767399, print 2009-11, no earlier online date) quote verbatim. human_genetic is in scope under decision 8; untested opening at the first case; product_in_model false and no dose entry are right.

Kelly 2015 quote verbatim; Zhou 2009 model_src resolves. Prospective 2009 to 2015, same direction_only on hyperglucagonaemia. Zhou's abstract states no glycaemic phenotype; the no-hypoglycaemia reading rests on Larger 2016 (PMC5118975, 2016-11-21, verified), which the note already treats as changing no status.

Guan 2015 (PMID 26373568, epub 2015-09-15) quote verbatim. The abstract says the model was built to explain MK-0893's dose-dependent LDL-C rise in T2D patients and reproduced it in dosed mice: a model that post-dates and is motivated by a class patient result and reproduces it is retro with retrodiction true (decision 10), not untested. MK-0893 is the same target and modality; decision 12 bars widening only to a sibling target. Track end state unchanged (14-16 stay prospective). Full text unreachable (PMC not OA subset, jlr.org 403), so the unnamed 'structurally diverse GRAs' could not be checked against MK-3577; product_in_model false stands on the named compound.
entries.adjudication_note: Decision 10: built after and motivated by MK-0893's human LDL-C rise, reproduced it: retro, retrodiction true. Decision 12 bars widening only to sibling targets or non-selective drugs; MK-0893 is the same selective mechanism and modality; retro never sets the headline.

Drafter should open it as its own model_id and score safety on it.

Compared with GRA-dosed patients it matches on hyperglucagonaemia and absence of hypoglycaemia (Kelly 2015); PNET risk untestable in 6-month trials. No track in the draft.

Guan 2015 J Lipid Res doi:10.1194/jlr.M060897 (online 2015-09-15): mouse model of GRA-induced LDL-C rise via cholesterol absorption, dosed with MK-0893 and 'structurally diverse GRAs'. A sibling-dosed model side is admissible (product_in_model false); it predates the member LDL-C findings (PF-06291874 Kazierad 2016, 2016-05-12; volagidemab Pettus 2022), so under decision 10 its first member comparison is a fresh prospective entry, not excluded by the member-only rule as the draft's safety #4 judgement says.
overall_note: All 17 entries confirmed: every DOI/URL resolves to the named document, every quote is verbatim (abstract-level except Pettus 2018 and the press item, seen in full), all registry dates verified against ClinicalTrials.gov v2. Corrections are the three missing model tracks, not any scored status.
could_not_verify: Full text of the paywalled Wiley/Elsevier papers (Peng 2014, Kelly 2015, Kazierad 2016/2018, Kazda 2016/2017, Guzman-Perez 2013, Mott 2024): quotes checked against abstracts only.
Whether Wiley posted Pettus 2018 as an accepted article on 2017-12-29 (draft's online date); Crossref and Europe PMC give 2018-01-22.
The original REMD Bio 2015 press release URL (only the Clinical Trials Arena reproduction was opened).

Models check: Guan 2015 full text (PMC4617405 not in the OA subset; jlr.org returns 403), so the identities of the 'structurally diverse GRAs' and whether any is MK-3577 remain unverified; also the paywalled Wiley/ADA full texts of Kelly 2015, Kazda 2016/2017, Kazierad 2016, Guzman 2017 and Conarello 2007 (abstracts only).
rule_questions: Decision 15: is an in-vivo pharmacological challenge in dosed humans (exogenous glucagon blocked, read as glucose/glucose production) 'direct' like an ex-vivo blockade of a stimulus, or 'downstream' because the readout is physiology? The draft calls it direct and admits the stricter reading.

Decision 10: does a post-hoc study run for another purpose (veterinary feline diabetes, Mott 2024) that neither cites nor is motivated by the human result qualify as a retrodiction track, or is it outside 'model systems compared with patients for the class' and should carry no entry?

Decision 12: when an on-target class harm (transaminases, LDL-C, BP, hyperglucagonaemia) is predicted or missed by modality-specific model systems, do the safety entries carry `modality` (as drafted) or stay pooled as the brief says for on-target harms?

Decisions 10 and 12: a model built to explain a non-member sibling's human harm (Guan 2015, MK-0893 LDL-C) that then anticipates the same harm with member drugs: is its first member comparison a prospective `same` (fresh entry after a retrodiction) or `retro`, given the retrodicted human result belongs to a drug outside the member list?
Decision 2, tier 5: does a trade-press article quoting the sponsor's statement count as the sponsor press release, or must the release itself (or an SEC filing) be the cited source?

Decision 4 (models check): does askable silence apply to a genetic characterisation model (Gcgr-/- knockout) as to a dosed tox package? ALT was measurable in mice and the knockout papers never reported it; patients showed dose-dependent aminotransferase rises (Kelly 2015). The draft leaves the knockout uncharged (safety 8) because its stated predictions govern.

Decision 7: may strengthens: true carry a second match on a track (same after same, safety 9/15/16), or is it reserved for a second miss that removes the first miss's excuse, with further matches going into patient_trials?

Decision 10 vs the member list: a class patient result from a same-mechanism, same-modality programme outside the tile's four members (MK-0893 LDL-C) motivated Guan 2015; the models check proposes retro for safety 13 on that reading, the drafter untested because MK-0893 is a non-member.
Decision 10 (models check): on an in-silico track built after the result (Tan 2025), should the opening untested entry carry retrodiction: true as well, or only the comparison entry?

Retrodiction anchor: Merck's hGCGR-mouse system published glucose lowering in 2004 (Qureshi 2004, doi:10.2337/diabetes.53.12.3267; Dallas-Yang 2004, doi:10.1016/j.ejphar.2004.08.023), before MK-0893's 2011 Phase 2, but the tracks pair Mu 2012. Does post-dating follow the paired model paper or the system's first public prediction (which would make efficacy 3/9/11 prospective same and model_first_use_year 2004)?

Safety retrodiction for a sibling-dosed model: safety 3's model claim (Guzman-Perez 2013, PF-06291874) post-dates the track drug LY2409021's own 2011 liver-enzyme result. Does 'the same drug's own patient result' mean the track's drug (retrodiction true) or the drug dosed in the model (false, as drafted)? Status is contra either way.

Model identity: Pfizer's rat glucagon challenge (Guzman-Perez 2013, PF-06291874) and Merck's hGCGR mouse/rhesus challenge (Mu 2012, GRA1) share model_id gcgr-sm-rodent-monkey-challenge; one system per sponsor package, or one small-molecule challenge system?
